findings.detail: Credit certifies base/inverse/reconstruction/elastic, queue and real scratch/reference quiescence. Wrapper controls all command/cache allocation. First cache beat consumes frame credit and partial preload retains reservation; start suppresses cache acceptance.

Public E captures size/epoch/ref/Qcache flags+FID/generation/all4 scheduling controls; children use only command registers at E+1. Pending masks stale status and data transfer eligibility, without resetting payload.

Current-owner fault and external reset/abort masks apply to public valid AND returned source-ready at pixel/reference/memory/coefficient/residual boundaries. Registered tagged peer kill does not delay these public masks; external abort remains immediate at private replay boundary.
Response ports remain unmasked; new credit requires ref_pending/scratch outstanding and all owners actually empty. No private flush/status can erase accepted physical service debt.

First current-owner cause is retained with reconstruction/inverse/coefficient priority; prior sticky faults are ignored during new command delivery. Sequence tag matches peer kill; max owner_sequence disables new credit.

Own producer coefficient/late-CRC fault does not register abort back into producer; held partial-cache abort can safely rearm despite stale retired owner_delivered. Both source findings were fixed before build rather than changing old oracles.

limitations: owner_sequence resets on reset; no new persistent reset-generation or echoed physical transaction ID. Local safety relies on synchronous flush, existing single-outstanding ordered/epoch service, and real drain before reuse. Complete production PCTL1/session protocol is unimplemented.

No current routed timing/throughput/board/CDCs/memory/panel/Sunshine/firmware/C2 publication qualification. Registered boundaries and all_available/credit/mask paths require future actual native measurements.
Source review and bounded focused campaigns are not formal all-history equivalence.
